:::{#thm-complement-null-space}
#### The orthogonal complement of a column space is a null space

For any $m \times n$ matrix $\matr{A}$,

$$
\mathcal{C}(\matr{A})^\perp = \mathcal{N}(\tp{\matr{A}}).
$$

:::

::: proof

Let $\vecf{a}_1, \ldots, \vecf{a}_n$ be the columns of $\matr{A}$,
so $\vecf{a}_j = (a_{1j}, \ldots, a_{mj})$.
For $\vecf{x} \in \reals^m$, entry $j$ of $\tp{\matr{A}} \vecf{x}$ is

$$
\ba
(\tp{\matr{A}} \vecf{x})_j
&= \sum_{i=1}^{m} (\tp{\matr{A}})_{ji}\, x_i
&& \text{(@def-matvec-mult)}
\\
&= \sum_{i=1}^{m} a_{ij}\, x_i
&& \text{(@def-matrix-transpose)}
\\
&= \vecf{a}_j \cdot \vecf{x}.
&& \text{(@def-dot-product)}
\ea
$$

So $\vecf{x} \in \mathcal{N}(\tp{\matr{A}})$ (@def-null-space)
exactly when $\vecf{a}_j \cdot \vecf{x} = 0$ for every column $\vecf{a}_j$.

**$\mathcal{C}(\matr{A})^\perp \subseteq \mathcal{N}(\tp{\matr{A}})$.**
Each column $\vecf{a}_j$ is in $\mathcal{C}(\matr{A})$ (@thm-column-space-span),
so a vector orthogonal to all of $\mathcal{C}(\matr{A})$
is orthogonal to every column.

**$\mathcal{N}(\tp{\matr{A}}) \subseteq \mathcal{C}(\matr{A})^\perp$.**
Suppose $\vecf{a}_j \cdot \vecf{x} = 0$ for every $j$,
and take any $\vecf{y} \in \mathcal{C}(\matr{A})$,
so $\vecf{y} = \matr{A} \vecf{z}$ for some $\vecf{z} \in \reals^n$
(@def-column-space).
The dot product is symmetric, $\vecf{u} \cdot \vecf{v} = \sum_i u_i v_i = \vecf{v} \cdot \vecf{u}$,
so the addition and scalar-multiplication rules
proved for the second slot in @thm-orthogonal-complement-subspace
hold for the first slot too.
Then

$$
\ba
\vecf{y} \cdot \vecf{x}
&= \paren{z_1 \vecf{a}_1 + \cdots + z_n \vecf{a}_n} \cdot \vecf{x}
&& \text{(@thm-matvec-columns)}
\\
&= z_1\,(\vecf{a}_1 \cdot \vecf{x}) + \cdots + z_n\,(\vecf{a}_n \cdot \vecf{x})
&& \text{(those two rules, in the first slot)}
\\
&= z_1 \cd 0 + \cdots + z_n \cd 0 = 0.
&& \text{(each } \vecf{a}_j \cdot \vecf{x} = 0 \text{)}
\ea
$$

So $\vecf{x}$ is orthogonal to every vector of $\mathcal{C}(\matr{A})$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-complement-null-space}
#### The complement of the column space in @exm-column-space

For $\matr{A}$ in @exm-column-space,
$\mathcal{C}(\matr{A}) = \operatorname{span}\cb{(1, 3)}$ (@exm-column-space-span).
Its transpose
$\tp{\matr{A}} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 3 \\ -2 & -6 \\ -2 & -6 \end{bmatrix}$
gives

$$
\tp{\matr{A}} \vecf{x}
= \paren{x_1 + 3x_2,\; -2\,(x_1 + 3x_2),\; -2\,(x_1 + 3x_2)},
$$

which is $\vzero_3$ exactly when $x_1 + 3x_2 = 0$,
that is, when $\vecf{x} = (-3x_2, x_2) = x_2\,(-3, 1)$.
So $\mathcal{N}(\tp{\matr{A}}) = \operatorname{span}\cb{(-3, 1)}$,
and by @thm-complement-null-space this line is $\mathcal{C}(\matr{A})^\perp$.
Directly: $c\,(1, 3) \cdot (-3, 1) = c\,(-3 + 3) = 0$.

:::
